items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: In the early records I made, sometimes Bunk and Jim Robinson would play a good deal together

ctx.x: I never heard of a single one. I would say if you're going to make it a very loose unison sometimes is about all.

The places I've heard it mostly has been later bands and mostly some of the white so-called Dixieland type bands where they harmonize together. To me, it isn't an interesting style. I mean, it's getting into the arranged, well, one of a better word, say, the Sousa march style or something else or any other written out popular tunes where you just write it all out in harmony because that's the big feature of the New Orleans, the independence of all those parts. In the early records I made, sometimes Bunk and Jim…

You know somebody was telling me and I didn't get this directly from Jim you might want to check up on this Jim now is supposed to be complaining because he has to play the melody because nobody else does you know and he then just swings back to the melody to help everybody

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1975-02-02
items.q: And we did go to see Jim Robinson, although we probably should have gone to see Vic.

ctx.x: Yeah, and probably hadn't heard Big Eye much since those days either. But, um, Bunk seemed to want to use Big Eye. And the, as soon as Bunk got into town that morning we went over to see Big Eye. We, I told him that Big Eye had taken sick the Saturday night before, and had to quit playing in the middle of the job that Saturday night. Uh, Mrs. Lutgen made him sit there on the stand throughout the night, though, to make it look like it was a bigger band. It was only about a three-piece band, maybe four pieces at…

I would have known it all over. This was downtown, all the way down to the Ninth Ward, where his son lives, which was out of his territory, more or less, you'd think, because he was an uptown man. Well, anyway, this is the one of the few times, at least we'll say, that Bunk's memory wasn't quite right. He said there's a clarinet player by the name of Stuart. I thought he said Strode or something at first, but it was just Bunk's heavy accent again. I'm sure he was saying the Stuart. Do you remember what the…

items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-07-13
items.q: And I made a recording, then the next recording I made with Bill Russell.

ctx.x: And I made a recording, I made a recording with, with, uh, with, uh, Kid Howard, Peter Bucca, Rudy Blush.
Mm-hmm. And I made a recording, then the next recording I made with Bill Russell.
Mm-hmm. No, you made the ones with Bill, but we made the ones with Rudy.
